video_caption: The video opens with a grey screen displaying white text, "Native advertising as Mashable see it" (Native advertising as Mashable sees it), which then transitions to a white screen. Subsequently, a blonde woman, identified by a text overlay as "Hannah Meium, Director of Branded Content, Mashable," appears seated in front of a white wall adorned with several orange and white circular logos of the "Native Advertising Institute." She is wearing a dark blue patterned turtleneck shirt, a ring on her left index finger, and a bracelet on her right wrist. She looks towards the viewer's left, speaking directly to the camera, using hand gestures to emphasize her points and occasionally smiling. The segment concludes with a transition back to a white screen displaying the question in black text: "What's a good example of native that your team did?".

In this video segment, a young woman with long blonde hair, wearing a dark blue top with maroon patterns, is speaking directly to the camera. She maintains an engaged and articulate expression, occasionally gesturing with her hands. The background is a white wall featuring a repeating logo of two "N"s forming an "M" or "W" shape within a red and orange gradient circle, accompanied by the text "Native Advertising Institute™". The first part of the segment shows a medium close-up of her face, with only a partial view of the text "Na Ad In". Around the 0:16 mark, the shot widens to a medium shot, revealing more of her body and the full "Native Advertising Institute™" text and logo repeated across the white background. The segment concludes with a title card asking, "What are the challenges for brand-publisher relationships?".

A young woman with blonde hair and blue eyes, wearing a dark long-sleeved top with a subtle pattern, speaks directly to the camera against a white background. Behind her, a circular logo in orange and red with yellow stylized "NAI" letters is visible, alongside the text "Native Advertising Institute™". She maintains a serious and engaged expression throughout, occasionally gesturing with her right hand. Around the 0:16 mark, the camera slightly zooms out to show more of her upper body and the full branding behind her, which includes repeated logos and the "Native Advertising Institute™" text. At 0:35, the scene cuts to a white screen displaying the question "What kind of information should publishers share with brands?" in black text, then cuts back to the woman in a close-up shot as she continues to speak.

The video opens with a fair-skinned woman with long, blonde hair, wearing a dark blue top with a red and brown pattern, speaking directly to the camera with a serious and engaged expression. She is positioned against a white wall with a repeating logo that features a stylized orange "NA" or "NN" within a red-orange circle, alongside the text "Native Advertising Institute™". As she continues to speak, the camera pulls back to show her seated, using her hands expressively with open palms and cupped gestures to emphasize her points. The background clearly displays multiple instances of the "Native Advertising Institute™" logo and full text. The shot then zooms back in on her face as she finishes her statement, maintaining her focused gaze. The scene transitions to a white screen displaying black text that reads, "Why do brands choose publishers over agencies for native?".

A blonde woman, wearing a dark blue high-necked top with a subtle red and brown abstract pattern, sits centered in the frame. Her hands are clasped in front of her as she speaks, occasionally gesturing slightly. She looks slightly to her right, maintaining eye contact. Behind her, a white wall is adorned with multiple circular logos for "Native Advertising Institute™" featuring an orange "NAi" icon within a red-orange ring. At 00:14, the shot zooms in, focusing on her upper body and face as she continues to speak expressively. The shot then zooms back out at 00:29 to the original framing. At 00:37, the video transitions to a plain white screen displaying black text that reads: "How do you scale premium native?".

A young woman with long blonde hair, wearing a dark top with a subtle reddish-brown pattern, speaks directly to the camera. She has blue eyes and is wearing small earrings. Her expression is earnest and she uses hand gestures to emphasize her points. Behind her, against a white wall, is the logo for the "Native Advertising Institute". The logo features a circular orange-yellow design with two stylized "N"s intersecting to form an "M" in the center. To the right of the logo, the words "Native Advertising Institute" are partially visible. In a slightly wider shot, it's clear that the logo and text are part of a repeating pattern on the wall, serving as a branded backdrop. She continues to speak and gesture, looking engaged in her explanation.

The video opens with a blonde woman, visible from the chest up, speaking directly to the camera. She has shoulder-length blonde hair and is wearing a dark long-sleeved shirt with a subtle, reddish-brown pattern. She maintains eye contact with the camera and uses hand gestures to emphasize her points. The background is a white wall adorned with multiple instances of a logo and text. The logo features an orange-yellow "NA" enclosed within a red circle, accompanied by the words "Native Advertising Institute™". At 00:25, the scene transitions to a plain white screen displaying the black text: "How do you make your audience appreciate native?" This question serves as a prompt, likely for the speaker or a discussion about native advertising.

A blonde woman with shoulder-length hair, wearing a dark blue long-sleeved top with a subtle reddish-brown abstract pattern, sits and speaks directly to the camera. She frequently uses hand gestures for emphasis. The background is a white wall adorned with multiple logos of the "Native Advertising Institute™", each featuring a stylized yellow "NAI" within an orange circle. The camera alternates between a medium shot, showing her upper body and the branded background clearly, and a closer shot focusing on her face and upper chest, with the background slightly blurred.

The video opens with a white screen displaying the question "How is the branded content studio organised at Mashable?" in black text. At 0:01, a fair-skinned woman with long, blonde hair, wearing a dark blue and red patterned long-sleeved top, is shown sitting and speaking. She is positioned against a white backdrop featuring multiple orange and red circular logos that contain intertwined "NAi" initials, which is also written as "Native Advertising Institute™". She explains that Mashable's branded content team is responsible for custom content and native advertising campaigns. She clarifies that this team operates under the overall umbrella of the content team, sharing the same leadership. She emphasizes the importance of this structure because their content adheres to the same standards and guidelines as the editorial team, but they maintain separation to prevent sponsored content from influencing editorial coverage. The video then transitions back to a white screen with a new question: "What are best practices for native campaigns on social media?"

The video opens with a white screen displaying the question "What are best practices for native campaigns on social media?". The scene then cuts to a medium shot of a woman with shoulder-length blonde hair, wearing a dark blue and red patterned long-sleeved top, sitting and speaking. She is positioned in front of a white wall adorned with a repeating logo: a yellow stylized "NAI" within a red circle, accompanied by the text "Native Advertising Institute™" (with "ising" from "Advertising" also visible on the right). She maintains eye contact and an engaged expression as she talks.

A young woman with blonde hair, wearing a dark gray patterned long-sleeved top with a high collar, speaks directly to someone slightly off-camera, gesturing with her hands while her mouth is open as she articulates her thoughts. Behind her, a white wall features the logo of the "Native Advertising Institute™," which consists of a circular red-orange outline enclosing two overlapping stylized yellow-orange "NA" letters, with the organization's full name partially visible beside it as "Nat Adv Ins" then clearly "Native Advertising Institute™". At 00:23, the shot widens to show the woman seated, continuing to speak and gesture with both hands, with the white wall now displaying multiple instances of the "Native Advertising Institute™" logo as a repeating background pattern. The video then transitions to a plain white screen displaying the question: "How do you suggest dealing with new social media platforms?".

A blonde woman with blue eyes, wearing a dark blue shirt with a red pattern, is speaking and gesturing to the camera. Initially, she is shown in a close-up, then the shot widens to reveal her sitting on a white stool or chair against a white wall. The wall is decorated with multiple orange and red circular logos that contain the white text "NAi" and "Native Advertising Institute™." She uses various hand gestures and facial expressions to emphasize her points throughout her speech. The video concludes with a white screen displaying the question "How do you label native on social media?" in black text.

The video opens with a medium shot of a woman with long blonde hair, wearing a dark blue and red patterned long-sleeved shirt. She is sitting and speaking directly to the camera, using hand gestures to emphasize her points. The background is a white wall featuring a repeating logo: two concentric circles (outer orange, inner red) with the letters "NAI" in yellow, next to the text "Native Advertising Institute™". She is speaking directly to the camera with a focused expression. Behind her, against a white wall, is a circular orange and yellow logo with the stylized letters "NAI" inside, and the partially visible text "Native Ad" next to it.
